canonical_statement: The review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tranexamic acid in revision total hip and knee arthroplasty and to assess the effects of administration dose and route, including septic revision cases.
Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty or revision total knee arthroplasty.

population.label: Adults undergoing rTHA or rTKA
inclusion_criteria: Revision total hip arthroplasty or revision total knee arthroplasty

canonical_statement: Eligible studies compared tranexamic acid treatment with non-tranexamic-acid treatment and reported efficacy or safety outcomes.
Randomized controlled trials and retrospective or prospective comparative studies were eligible, with no restriction on tranexamic acid administration route.

population.label: Comparative studies of TXA in revision hip or knee arthroplasty
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trial, retrospective comparative study, or prospective comparative study

canonical_statement: Reviews, animal studies, case reports, correspondence, conference or poster abstracts, and articles without original data were excluded.
The intervention of interest was perioperative tranexamic acid administered to patients undergoing revision hip or knee arthroplasty.

exposures.details: Perioperative administration; route unrestricted by eligibility criteria

canonical_statement: The comparator was no tranexamic acid treatment.
Efficacy outcomes included change in hemoglobin, calculated blood loss, blood transfusion rate, and red blood cell transfusion units per patient.

outcome.definition: Hemoglobin change, calculated blood loss, blood transfusion rate, and RBC transfusion units per patient

canonical_statement: Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and aggregate venous thromboembolism complications.

outcome.definition: DVT, PE, and aggregate VTE complications

canonical_statement: The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, Embase, and Web of Science from database inception through 2024 and also checked references of included studies.
The systematic review and meta-analysis was designed according to PRISMA and was registered in PROSPERO as CRD420251129117.
Two reviewers independently screened potentially relevant full texts and extracted data; disagreements were resolved by a third reviewer.
Two reviewers assessed study quality using Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Tools, with disagreements resolved by consensus with a third reviewer.
Meta-analysis used R version 4.5.0, random-effects pooling, weighted mean differences or relative measures, and 95% confidence intervals; at least three studies were required for a meta-analysis.
Heterogeneity was assessed with I-squared, categorized as very low (0-25%), low (25-50%), medium (50-75%), and high (>75%).

The authors performed leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses for septic revision and dose or route, and publication-bias assessment using funnel plots and Egger's tests; statistical significance was defined as P<0.05.
The review included 27 studies with 10,248 patients: 4,700 received tranexamic acid and 5,548 were in non-tranexamic-acid groups.

population.label: Patients in 27 included revision arthroplasty studies

canonical_statement: Sixteen included studies reported revision total hip arthroplasty and 12 reported revision total knee arthroplasty; two studies reported both joints separately.
Twenty-five of the 27 included studies contributed to meta-analysis; one study lacked joint-specific data and one lacked control-group data.

In revision total hip arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced the postoperative hemoglobin drop by a pooled weighted mean difference of 0.79 g/dL versus no tranexamic acid (WMD -0.79, 95% CI -1.22 to -0.36; P=0.016; I²=0%).

In revision total knee arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced the postoperative hemoglobin drop by a pooled weighted mean difference of 0.64 g/dL versus no tranexamic acid (WMD -0.64, 95% CI -1.27 to -0.02; P=0.048; I²=57.8%).
In revision total hip arthroplasty, calculated blood loss was not significantly lower with tranexamic acid (WMD -326.18 mL, 95% CI -655.07 to 2.72; P=0.051; I²=71.8%).

population.label: rTHA patients in 4 studies contributing 5 intervention groups

canonical_statement: In the review's report of Reichel et al., revision total knee arthroplasty patients receiving tranexamic acid had lower calculated blood loss than controls (2916±1226 mL vs 3611±1474 mL; mean difference -695 mL; P=0.001).

population.label: rTKA patients in Reichel et al. (2018), as reported by the review

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced blood transfusion risk (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.71; P<0.001; I²=91.1%).

population.label: rTHA patients in 14 studies contributing 16 intervention groups

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced red blood cell units transfused per patient (WMD -0.98 units, 95% CI -1.53 to -0.44; P=0.006; I²=48.6%).

concept.text: Red blood cell transfusion units per patient

canonical_statement: In revision total knee arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced blood transfusion risk (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.75; P=0.012; I²=69.5%).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, tranexamic acid reduced red blood cell units transfused per patient (WMD -0.49 units, 95% CI -0.67 to -0.31; P=0.007; I²=0%).

concept.text: Red blood cell transfusion units per patient

canonical_statement: Among septic revision total hip arthroplasty cases, calculated blood loss did not differ significantly between tranexamic acid and no-tranexamic-acid groups (WMD -1116.41 mL, 95% CI -2386.60 to 153.78; P=0.085).
Among septic revision total hip arthroplasty cases, tranexamic acid reduced transfusion risk (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.91; P=0.001).
In revision total hip arthroplasty, tranexamic acid was not associated with a significant difference in total venous thromboembolism complications (RR 1.25, 95% CI 0.75 to 2.07; P=0.341; I²=0%).
In revision total hip arthroplasty, tranexamic acid was not associated with a significant difference in pulmonary embolism (RR 1.96, 95% CI 0.10 to 40.23; P=0.441; I²=1.2%).

For deep vein thrombosis in revision total hip arthroplasty, one included study reported similar incidence between tranexamic acid and control groups (P=0.58), while another reported 6 versus 4 events without a significance test.
In revision total knee arthroplasty, tranexamic acid was not associated with a significant difference in total venous thromboembolism complications (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.14 to 3.76; P=0.494; I²=0%).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, tranexamic acid was not associated with a significant difference in deep vein thrombosis (RR 1.59, 95% CI 0.90 to 2.89; P=0.072; I²=0%).
Two studies of septic revision total hip arthroplasty reported no difference in venous thromboembolism rate between tranexamic acid and no-tranexamic-acid groups.

In revision total hip arthroplasty, combined intravenous plus intra-articular tranexamic acid did not significantly differ from intravenous-only tranexamic acid in calculated blood loss (WMD 162.23 mL, 95% CI -109.48 to 433.93; P=0.2419).

concept.text: Combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, combined intravenous plus intra-articular tranexamic acid did not significantly differ from intravenous-only tranexamic acid in transfusion risk (RR 0.61, 95% CI 0.29 to 1.27; P=0.1884).

concept.text: Combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, combined intravenous plus intra-articular tranexamic acid did not significantly differ from intravenous-only tranexamic acid in total thromboembolism (RR 1.22, 95% CI 0.41 to 3.59; P=0.724).

concept.text: Combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, single-dose intravenous tranexamic acid reduced transfusion risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.54 to 0.78; P<0.001).
In revision total hip arthroplasty, double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid reduced transfusion risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.75; P<0.001).
Within the 2-g double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid subgroup for revision total hip arthroplasty, transfusion risk was reduced versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.84; P=0.0068).
In revision total hip arthroplasty, double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid reduced calculated blood loss versus no tranexamic acid (WMD -407.63 mL, 95% CI -645.01 to -170.26; P=0.0008).

population.label: rTHA double-dose IV TXA blood-loss subgroup

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid did not significantly change pulmonary embolism risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.15 to 4.74; P=0.851).

population.label: rTHA double-dose IV TXA safety subgroup

canonical_statement: In revision total hip arthroplasty, double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid did not significantly change deep vein thrombosis risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.32 to 3.14; P=0.999).

population.label: rTHA double-dose IV TXA safety subgroup

canonical_statement: In revision total knee arthroplasty, intravenous tranexamic acid reduced transfusion risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.70; P<0.001).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid reduced transfusion risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.45, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.80; P=0.0063).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, intravenous tranexamic acid did not significantly change deep vein thrombosis risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 1.37, 95% CI 0.34 to 5.57; P=0.663).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, intravenous tranexamic acid did not significantly change pulmonary embolism risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.12 to 2.65; P=0.459).
In revision total knee arthroplasty, intravenous tranexamic acid did not significantly change total venous thromboembolism risk versus no tranexamic acid (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.21 to 2.35; P=0.573).
Egger's regression test found no significant small-study effect for the revision total hip arthroplasty blood-transfusion-rate analysis (P=0.455).
JBI appraisal totals for the five included randomized controlled trials ranged from 9 to 11 out of 13.
JBI appraisal totals for the included cohort studies ranged from 7 to 10 out of 11.

In the review's supplementary synthesis of revision total hip arthroplasty, multidose oral tranexamic acid did not differ significantly from single-dose IV, double-dose IV, or combined IV-IA regimens for hemoglobin difference, calculated blood loss, or transfusion rate (P=0.912, 0.794, and 0.955, respectively).

In the review's supplementary synthesis of revision total knee arthroplasty, one four-regimen study found a significant difference in hemoglobin drop across single IV, double IV, combined IV-IA, and multidose oral tranexamic acid groups (P=0.001), but no significant differences in calculated blood loss (P=0.65) or transfusion rate (P=0.955).

In two study-level revision total knee arthroplasty comparisons summarized by the review, intra-articular tranexamic acid reduced transfusion rates versus no tranexamic acid (25% vs 52.5%, P=0.05; and 7.9% vs 37.1%, P<0.001).

In one study summarized by the review, combined intravenous plus intra-articular tranexamic acid was superior to intra-articular-only tranexamic acid for hemoglobin drop (2.7 vs 3.7, P<0.001), transfusion rate (10.2% vs 40%, P=0.013), and RBC units (0.2 vs 0.7, P=0.007), with no significant thromboembolic difference (P=0.407).

In the Chen et al. study summarized by the review, 1-g, 2-g, and at-least-3-g intravenous tranexamic acid regimens had transfusion rates of 17%, 21%, and 7.1%, respectively (P=0.208), with VTE complication rates of 2.4%, 0%, and 0%.

The authors concluded that tranexamic acid should be routinely considered in revision total hip and knee arthroplasty because it reduces transfusion rates and hemoglobin drop without increasing VTE, DVT, or PE.
The authors concluded that current evidence does not establish superiority of a specific tranexamic acid dosing regimen or administration route in revision arthroplasty.
The authors concluded that tranexamic acid may reduce transfusion rates in septic revision arthroplasty without clear safety concerns, but the evidence is limited.
For general revision THA and TKA, the authors proposed that tranexamic acid be used to reduce transfusion rates, hemoglobin drop, and RBC transfusion units, rating the evidence as strong.
For general revision THA and TKA, the authors proposed that tranexamic acid does not increase VTE, PE, or DVT risk, rating the evidence as moderate.
The authors proposed that no single- versus double-dose intravenous tranexamic acid regimen is clearly superior in revision arthroplasty; they rated the evidence as limited.

The authors proposed that intravenous-only and combined intravenous plus intra-articular tranexamic acid routes have no clearly superior option in revision arthroplasty; they rated the evidence as limited.
For septic revision arthroplasty, the authors proposed that tranexamic acid reduces transfusion without clear safety concerns, rating the evidence as limited.

For septic revision arthroplasty, the authors proposed that tranexamic acid does not increase VTE, PE, or DVT risk, while noting that this was based on individual study reports rather than meta-analytic support; evidence was rated limited.
For septic revision arthroplasty, the authors noted that only intravenous tranexamic acid had been studied and rated the route evidence as moderate.
The authors stated that no definitive optimal tranexamic acid protocol combining dose and route could be recommended and that further randomized trials are required.
The authors identified heterogeneity among included studies as a limitation that may account for variation in blood-loss and postoperative-complication outcomes.
The authors noted that concurrent use of tranexamic acid and prophylactic anticoagulants in some patient groups may have influenced blood-loss and venous-thromboembolism outcomes.
Evidence comparing tranexamic acid dosing regimens and routes in revision arthroplasty was limited, so conclusions about an optimal dose or route remain uncertain.
A meta-analysis of tranexamic acid effects on calculated blood loss in revision total knee arthroplasty was not feasible because too few studies reported the outcome.
Safety evidence in septic revision arthroplasty was limited; the review could not meta-analyze venous thromboembolism in septic rTHA and relied on two individual studies reporting no difference.
The authors declared that there were no conflicts of interest.
